# WP3 — the pitch × burst interaction

**Status:** WP3 deliverable of [`docs/dop3000/sparse-pass-analysis-plan.md`](../../docs/dop3000/sparse-pass-analysis-plan.md) §4, generated by `udv-sparse-pitch-burst` against the revision `9eb11ae`. Regenerate with

```bash
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m udv_echo_process.cli sparse-pitch-burst \
    --analysis-commit <generator>
```

**What it measures.** The four corners of the pass's pitch × burst design, on one common knot set: `cc1` (0.6167 mm, burst 4) and `cc3` (2.96 mm, burst 4) inside the `burst-4` job, `cc2` (0.6167 mm, burst 18) and `cc4` (2.96 mm, burst 18) inside `burst-18`. The endpoint is the difference of differences

```text
I(z) = [v(0.617,18)(z) - v(2.96,18)(z)] - [v(0.617,4)(z) - v(2.96,4)(z)]
```

per common knot, reduced to the **unweighted mean over the knots**, with the four corner contrasts (the simple effects) beside it. Which `cc*` belongs to which job and carries which pitch and burst is **read from the decoded recordings** and re-checked against the plan, not assumed.

**What it does not claim.** No causation: every number is an observed difference between recordings. No significance test, no confidence interval, no statement below the anchors' own ~10-12 mm/s. No emissions statement (WP4), no reference-condition statement (that is CR1-CR4's, WP2), and no new acquisition.

## The crossed cells

Primary window 12 s (100 nominal revolutions), common support 10.138–98.938 mm, common knots 31 at 2.9600 mm, statistic `mean` (the per-gate window mean every slice here reduces from).

| pitch (mm) | burst 4 | burst 18 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.617 | `cc1` 30.291 | `cc2` 25.973 |
| 2.96 | `cc3` 23.970 | `cc4` 27.519 |

| `cc1` | burst-4 | 0.616667 | 4 | 145 | 145 | 29.757 | 2 | ctrl-begin → ctrl-mid |
| `cc2` | burst-18 | 0.616667 | 18 | 145 | 145 | 25.384 | 8 | ctrl-begin → ctrl-mid |
| `cc3` | burst-4 | 2.960000 | 4 | 31 | 31 | 23.970 | 4 | ctrl-mid → ctrl-end |

## Each corner beside its block-local anchors

The 1.85 mm anchor controls are **context, not cells**: they never enter `I(z)`. They are printed here so a reader sees where each corner sits relative to the movement its own job recorded.

| corner | job | corner mean (own gates, mm/s) | vs B | vs M | vs E | job anchor spread (mm/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cc1` | burst-4 | 30.291 | +0.625 | +1.859 | +10.271 | 9.646 |
| `cc2` | burst-18 | 25.973 | -1.663 | -9.154 | +2.827 | 11.980 |
| `cc3` | burst-4 | 23.970 | -5.697 | -4.463 | +3.949 | 9.646 |
| `cc4` | burst-18 | 27.519 | -0.116 | -7.607 | +4.373 | 11.980 |

The anchor means those differences are taken against, and each job's structure:

- `burst-4` — burst 4, emissions 20, B - CC1 - M - CC3 - E: B (ctrl-begin) 29.666, M (ctrl-mid) 28.432, E (ctrl-end) 20.020 mm/s; anchor spread 9.646 mm/s (WP1, each burst job's own block-local anchor spread).
- `burst-18` — burst 18, emissions 20, B - CC2 - M - CC4 - E: B (ctrl-begin) 27.635, M (ctrl-mid) 35.126, E (ctrl-end) 23.146 mm/s; anchor spread 11.980 mm/s (WP1, each burst job's own block-local anchor spread).

These differences are **grid-mismatched by construction and are not residuals**: a corner's scalar is the mean over its own 145 or 31 gates at its own pitch, an anchor's is the mean over 49 gates at 1.85 mm. They place the corner inside its block; they enter no interaction and screen against nothing.

## The alignment rule, and why nothing is interpolated

- The knots are the 2.96 mm measurement's **own native supported gate depths** — 31 gates, 10.138–98.938 mm, step 2.9600 mm — which is the coarsest grid this design measures. The knot set is not chosen here: it is what that recording measured.
- Every corner is read at its **nearest native gate** to each knot. No interpolation, no resampling, no fit: a resampled coarse profile would manufacture structure the 2.96 mm grid never resolved, and an upsampled one would hide the width of the gates the fine grid actually averaged.
- Per knot the native depth actually used and its offset from the knot are published in `pitch-burst.csv` and `pitch-burst.json`.
- The largest offset this run needed is **0.246667 mm** (`cc1` at knot 17 = 60.458 mm); the 2.96 mm corners carry offset 0 by construction.
- **Fail-closed:** an offset above half the coarse pitch (1.4800 mm) refuses with a named error and writes nothing, because a gate that far from its knot is not the same depth as the knot.

## The floors, and which endpoint applies where

| quantity | endpoint | value | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| depth-resolved magnitude (`\|I(z)\|` per knot, a contrast's per-knot magnitude) | WP2's per-depth endpoint | **14.603 mm/s** at 21.238 mm | WP2, the cr3-cr4 pair, per-depth window-mean difference |
| scalar / depth-averaged effect (the reduction over the knots) | WP2's depth-averaged endpoint | **4.235 mm/s** | WP2's depth-averaged endpoint, the same pair |
| conservative guard | each burst job's own block-local anchor spread | **9.646** mm/s (`burst-4`) and **11.980** mm/s (`burst-18`) | WP1, each burst job's own block-local anchor spread |

The two WP2 endpoints are different quantities measured from the same pair of reference runs, and this slice never mixes them: a per-knot magnitude is screened against 14.603 mm/s, a scalar against 4.235 mm/s.

## The conservative reading

Both burst jobs' own anchors move by **9.646 mm/s** (`burst-4`) and **11.980 mm/s** (`burst-18`) inside their own job. A pitch or burst effect smaller than ~10-12 mm/s is therefore **not resolvable in this pass**: it cannot be separated from the anchors' own movement in those jobs.

- The scalar reduction of `I(z)` is **-7.922 mm/s**. Its magnitude is 7.922 mm/s, which is below both anchor floors (9.646 and 11.980 mm/s) and also below the depth-resolved endpoint: at the depth-averaged level this interaction is not separable from the two jobs' own anchor movement.
- Depth-resolved, `|I(z)|` is a screening outcome above the `burst-4` guard at **14 of 31 knots (45.2 %)** and above the `burst-18` guard at **10 of 31 (32.3 %)**.
- Against WP2's depth-resolved endpoint (14.603 mm/s), `|I(z)|` is a screening outcome above it at **9 of 31 knots (29.0 %)**.

So the honest reading of this pass is: the interaction is concentrated in the near and mid field, where its local magnitudes reach 21.743 mm/s at 45.658 mm and change sign around the middle of the profile, while its depth-averaged value stays inside the anchors' own movement. Both statements are observations. Neither proves that the pitch, the burst or their combination caused anything — the two jobs differ in condition *and* in their own drift, and this pass has one realization per corner.

## What is checked before a run is published

The command refuses — non-zero exit, named reason, nothing written — for anything the frozen WP0 ingest refuses, for a corner that is missing, duplicated or not the plan's declared condition, for coarse corners whose native grids disagree, for a knot grid that is not the coarse pitch, and for an alignment offset beyond half the coarse pitch. It then publishes only when every structural check below holds:

| check | holds |
|---|---|
| `all_four_corners_are_read_at_native_gates` | yes |
| `anchor_floors_reproduce_wp1` | yes |
| `anchors_excluded_from_the_interaction` | yes |
| `corner_conditions_are_the_plans_declared_pitch_and_burst` | yes |
| `corners_share_one_emissions_level` | yes |
| `engine_revision_recorded` | yes |
| `four_corners_present` | yes |
| `interaction_recomputes_from_the_published_corner_profiles` | yes |
| `knots_are_the_coarse_grids_native_supported_gates` | yes |
| `no_alignment_offset_beyond_half_the_coarse_pitch` | yes |
| `the_four_contrasts_carry_the_interaction` | yes |
| `the_two_screening_endpoints_are_kept_apart` | yes |
| `window_and_support_are_the_wp0_ones` | yes |

## What is deliberately not here

- **No causation claim.** Every number is an observed difference between recordings of a moving rig. One realization per corner, no replicate, no significance test: nothing here says the pitch, the burst or their combination *produced* the difference.
- **The anchors are not cells.** `ctrl-begin`/`ctrl-mid`/`ctrl-end` record the 1.85 mm reference window at their own job's condition; they are neither factorial cell nor input to `I(z)`, and they are published only as the context a corner sits in.
- **No claim below ~10-12 mm/s.** The two burst jobs' own anchor floors are 9.646 and 11.980 mm/s, so a pitch or burst effect of that size or smaller cannot be separated from the anchors' movement inside the jobs. Nothing in this slice asserts it.
- **No new acquisition.** The pass is closed; this slice reads its committed bytes and changes no recording, log, manifest or plan.
- **No change to the frozen artefacts.** WP0's table, WP1's anchor floors and WP2's reference floor are read, never rewritten; the 1.85 mm window appears here only as the anchors' context, because no 1.85 mm corner is a cell of this 2x2.
- **No emissions statement** (WP4) and **no reference-condition statement** (WP2's CR1-CR4 alone).
